sections.title: Finance – Xero
sections.html:
Overview

ORN Europe pays European suppliers on behalf of ORN Australia’s bookings. Each month we recharge those costs to ORN Australia with a 10% mark-up, invoiced through Xero. Raj makes the payment himself based on our statement. We then reconcile what we have paid against the supplier bills.

PartyRole
ORN Europe LimitedPays suppliers; raises the invoice and statement in Xero
ORN AustraliaCustomer billed for the recharged costs plus 10%
Raj KumarReviews the statement and makes the payment to ORN Europe
SuppliersIssue the bills that support every paid amount

Monthly process

Step 1 – Load paid amounts

  1. Export or list every supplier payment made for ORN Australia bookings in the month (bank feed in Xero, card statements, transfer confirmations).
  2. For each payment, record: date paid, supplier, Nexus booking reference, guest / TAG reference, currency, amount paid, and the GBP equivalent if paid in another currency.
  3. Enter each payment in Xero as a spend money transaction or bill payment against the supplier, coded to [ACCOUNT CODE], with the booking reference in the reference field.

Step 2 – Apply the 10% mark-up and invoice ORN Australia

  1. Total the paid amounts for the period.
  2. Raise one sales invoice in Xero to ORN Australia. Either one line per booking, or one line for the total cost plus a separate mark-up line. [CONFIRM PREFERRED FORMAT]
  3. Mark-up = 10% of the paid amount. Invoice total = paid amount × 1.10.
  4. Attach the payment schedule (Step 1 list) to the invoice in Xero.
  5. Currency of invoice: [GBP / AUD / EUR – CONFIRM]. VAT treatment: [CONFIRM WITH ACCOUNTANT].

Step 3 – Send the statement

  1. Send the invoice and a Xero customer statement to Raj, showing opening balance, new invoice, payments received and closing balance.
  2. Raj makes the payment himself based on that statement.

Step 4 – Record the payment

  1. When the funds arrive, match the receipt in the Xero bank feed to the ORN Australia invoice.
  2. Any difference (bank charges, FX) is coded to [ACCOUNT CODE] and noted on the next statement.

Step 5 – Reconcile against supplier bills

  1. Obtain the supplier bill or invoice for every amount paid. Attach it in Xero to the matching payment.
  2. Check that each bill matches the amount paid and the booking reference. Flag differences: overpayment, underpayment, credit notes due, refunds or cancellations.
  3. Carry any refund or credit due to ORN Australia onto the next month’s invoice as a negative line.
  4. Payments still without a bill go on a “bills outstanding” list, which is chased weekly.

Worked example

BookingSupplierPaid (£)Mark-up 10% (£)Invoiced (£)
NEX-10001Hotel, Paris4,000.00400.004,400.00
NEX-10002Van transport, Rome2,500.00250.002,750.00
NEX-10003Attraction tickets500.0050.00550.00
Total7,000.00700.007,700.00

Illustrative figures only. In reconciliation, if the Paris hotel bill later shows £3,850 (a £150 credit), the £150 plus its £15 mark-up is credited to ORN Australia on the next invoice.

sections.title: EU operations
sections.html:
How the operation runs

  • Live from 1 August 2026. Every European booking is tracked, reconfirmed and confirmed in the Europe Operations & Reconfirmation Hub (orngroup.github.io/ornoperations/).
  • Australia loads bookings from Nexus; they appear on the “New Bookings” tab for the UK/EU team. Ken, Tim and Suman reconfirm each component against the 6-point check (operator, contact, confirmation, time, pick-up location).
  • Once all components pass, the booking moves to the “6-point confirmed” tab and Australia can download the client-facing confirmation/travel voucher themselves.

Option 1 – keep everything where it is (recommended)

The simplest handover is to make Raj an owner of the orngroup GitHub account. Every site keeps running at the same address and nothing needs re-importing.

  1. Raj creates a GitHub account at github.com/signup (if he has none).
  2. Ajay goes to github.com/orgs/orngroup/people → Invite member → enters Raj’s username → role Owner.
  3. Raj accepts the email invitation.
  4. Do the same for each Firebase project: console.firebase.google.com → project → Settings → Users and permissions → Add member → role Owner.

If orngroup is a personal account rather than an organisation, use Settings → Collaborators on each repository, or transfer the repositories to Raj (Settings → General → Danger zone → Transfer).

Option 2 – rebuild a site from a zip in a new GitHub account

  1. Download the zip from this section (or the Google Drive folder) and unzip it on your computer.
  2. Sign in to GitHub and click New repository. Use the same name as before (e.g. ornoperations). Set it to Public, then Create repository.
  3. On the empty repository page click uploading an existing file. Drag in the contents of the unzipped folder – the files and sub-folders, not the zip itself. Click Commit changes.
  4. If the site has many files, the web uploader may stop (limit about 100 files per upload, 25 MB per file). Use GitHub Desktop instead: File → Add local repository → Publish.
  5. Go to Settings → Pages. Under Source choose “Deploy from a branch”, branch main, folder /(root), then Save.
  6. Wait one to two minutes. The site appears at https://YOUR-USERNAME.github.io/REPOSITORY-NAME/.
  7. Check the site opens and logs in. Firebase-backed sites keep using the same Firebase project, so data is unaffected.

Option 3 – copy a repository that is still online

While the orngroup repositories are still live, any repository can be copied in one step: go to github.com/new/import, paste the old repository URL (e.g. https://github.com/orngroup/ornoperations), choose the new owner and name, and start the import. Then switch on Pages as in step 5 above.

Custom domains

brandon.hospro.co.uk and www.orn.group point at GitHub through DNS. If a site moves to a new GitHub account: add the domain under Settings → Pages → Custom domain, then change the DNS CNAME record at the domain registrar to YOUR-USERNAME.github.io.

Uploading the zips here

Use Admin → Upload documents, choose the section “GitHub files” and add one zip per repository. Files up to about 50 MB each upload reliably.
